events.title: First Gaines County cases confirmed
events.detail: South Plains Public Health District announced two confirmed measles cases in Gaines County, Texas — both unvaccinated school-aged children hospitalized in Lubbock. This was the seed event for what became the largest US measles outbreak since elimination was declared in 2000.

events.title: Texas declares Gaines County outbreak
events.detail: Texas Department of State Health Services formally declared a measles outbreak in Gaines County with 6 confirmed cases, all unvaccinated school-aged children concentrated in the close-knit, undervaccinated Mennonite community. Gaines County's kindergarten MMR vaccination rate was roughly 82%, well below the 95% herd-immunity threshold.

events.title: Cases quadruple to 24 including adults
events.detail: One week after the outbreak declaration, confirmed cases jumped from 6 to 24, including the first two adult cases, signaling spread beyond the initial school-age cluster.

events.title: First US measles death since 2015
events.detail: An unvaccinated school-aged child died of measles in Lubbock, the first US measles death in a decade and the first fatality of the West Texas outbreak. The child had no known underlying conditions.

events.title: Outbreak spreads to New Mexico and Oklahoma
events.detail: Genetically linked cases confirmed in New Mexico (centered on Lea County, bordering Gaines County) and Oklahoma, as RFK Jr. told Fox News' Sean Hannity that outbreaks could be partly driven by 'waning immunity' from vaccination — a claim public health experts rejected.

events.title: Vitamin A toxicity emerges among unvaccinated children
events.detail: Covenant Children's Hospital in Lubbock confirmed fewer than ten pediatric measles patients developed abnormal liver function from vitamin A toxicity, after HHS Secretary RFK Jr. directed CDC to promote vitamin A alongside measles guidance. Experts noted WHO's vitamin A guidance targets malnourished populations abroad and does not apply to West Texas.

events.title: Unvaccinated adult dies in New Mexico
events.detail: An unvaccinated adult in Lea County, New Mexico died of measles, becoming the second confirmed fatality of the outbreak and the first adult death.

events.title: RFK Jr. sworn in as HHS Secretary
events.detail: Robert F. Kennedy Jr., a longtime vaccine skeptic, was sworn in as Secretary of Health and Human Services, taking direct oversight of the federal response to the growing West Texas measles outbreak.

events.title: Second Texas child dies; RFK Jr. visits outbreak zone
events.detail: Eight-year-old Daisy Hildebrand of Gaines County died April 3 of measles-related pulmonary failure, with no underlying health conditions. RFK Jr. visited the outbreak area shortly after and, amid the deadly outbreak, publicly urged parents to vaccinate — a rare direct pro-vaccine statement that drew backlash from his anti-vaccine supporter base.

events.title: West Virginia governor orders religious exemption process
events.detail: Gov. Patrick Morrisey issued Executive Order 7-25 directing state health officials to establish a religious-exemption process for school vaccine mandates, even as the legislature's House voted down a broader religious/philosophical exemption bill. About 300 exemptions were granted under the new administrative policy by late May.

events.title: RFK Jr. dismisses entire CDC vaccine advisory committee
events.detail: HHS Secretary Kennedy fired all 17 members of the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) on June 9, 2025, saying the move was needed so the Trump administration could appoint a majority of new members before 2028. Newly appointed members later voted to narrow MMRV and hepatitis B recommendations.

events.title: CDC Director Susan Monarez fired after 28 days
events.detail: The White House fired Senate-confirmed CDC Director Susan Monarez after she refused RFK Jr.'s demand to preemptively accept ACIP vaccine-policy recommendations and fire career vaccine officials. Her ouster, which she said amounted to Kennedy 'weaponizing public health,' triggered a wave of senior CDC resignations, including chief medical officer Dr. Debra Houry.

events.title: Texas declares West Texas outbreak over
events.detail: Texas DSHS announced the end of the West Texas measles outbreak, with 762 total cases confirmed since late January and two pediatric deaths. The outbreak had spread to New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Kansas via the tightly linked Mennonite community network.

events.title: ACIP votes to restrict combined MMRV shot
events.detail: The reconstituted ACIP voted 8-3 to stop recommending the combined MMRV (measles-mumps-rubella-varicella) shot for children under 4, instead recommending separate MMR and varicella shots — reviving a debate last settled over a decade ago. Medical groups including the AMA and AAP criticized the process.

era: Elimination Status Threatened & National Spread (Oct 2025 – Aug 2026)

events.title: South Carolina outbreak grows toward 1,000 cases
events.detail: A new outbreak took hold in South Carolina between October 2025 and March 2026, eventually totaling nearly 1,000 cases — most among unvaccinated people — making the state the new national epicenter.

events.title: Americas region loses measles elimination status
events.detail: PAHO's Measles, Rubella, and Congenital Rubella Syndrome Elimination Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission, meeting in Mexico City Nov 4-7, concluded the Region of the Americas lost its measles-elimination status after endemic transmission persisted in Canada for over 12 months. As of Nov 7, 12,596 confirmed cases had been reported across 10 countries in the region (a 30-fold increase over 2024), with 28 deaths — 23 in Mexico, 3 in the US, 2 in Canada. Losing status in any one country triggers loss for the whole region; CDC began assessing whether the US itself would separately lose its 2000 elimination designation.

events.title: Utah outbreak begins, becomes state's largest in 40 years
events.detail: A measles outbreak took hold in Utah in mid-2025 near the Utah-Arizona border and grew into the state's largest in four decades, eventually surpassing 700 combined cases by mid-2026. Of 602 cases analyzed in a NEJM Evidence report, 49 patients (8%) were hospitalized, 90% of them unvaccinated; 55% of hospitalized patients had abnormal chest X-rays and 29% were diagnosed with pneumonia.

events.title: US measles cases top 2,000 for the year, highest in 30+ years
events.detail: CDC's year-end tally for 2025 reached 2,289 confirmed cases across 48 outbreaks, with 90% (2,066 of 2,289) outbreak-associated — the highest annual US total since 1991, before elimination was declared.

events.title: Acting CDC Director O'Neill calls to split MMR shot
events.detail: Acting CDC Director Jim O'Neill, who was never Senate-confirmed, publicly called to 'break up' the combined MMR vaccine into three separate shots and questioned the shot's safety amid the still-expanding outbreak (1,136 cases confirmed as of Feb 26, 2026). O'Neill was removed by RFK Jr. days later, on Feb 14, 2026, leaving the agency without a director.

events.title: 2026 case total surpasses all of 2025
events.detail: By late July 2026, the year's confirmed case count (2,371 across 45 jurisdictions, 94% outbreak-associated) had already exceeded the full-year 2025 total of 2,289, confirming 2026 as the worst measles year since 1991 with months still remaining.

events.title: Trump signs executive order to split MMR vaccine
events.detail: President Trump signed an executive order directing that the combined MMR vaccine 'should be administered in three separate single-disease shots once such products are domestically available,' as part of a broader 'Gold Standard Childhood Vaccine Recommendations' policy lowering universally recommended childhood shots from 17 to 11. No single-disease measles, mumps, or rubella vaccines are currently sold in the US; HHS has 90 days to present a plan. Trump linked the combined shot to autism, a claim with no scientific support. Medical groups said the order is likely to face legal challenges.

events.title: Kindergarten vaccine exemptions hit record high nationwide
events.detail: CDC's SchoolVaxView data for the 2025-2026 school year, released Aug 17, 2026, showed exemptions from one or more vaccines among US kindergartners rose to 4.2% (from 3.6%), with 24 states above 5% and exemptions increasing in 41 states plus DC. National MMR coverage slipped to 92.4% from 92.5%, staying below the 95% threshold needed to prevent outbreaks; about 280,000 kindergartners started school without complete two-dose MMR documentation. Coverage ranged from 98.9% in West Virginia to 75.2% in Idaho.

events.title: RFK Jr. tells CNN parents should vaccinate against measles
events.detail: With cases at a 35-year high, HHS Secretary RFK Jr. told CNN parents should vaccinate their children against measles, even as he continued to disparage the MMR vaccine elsewhere as 'leaky' with declining immunity — the latest instance of what FactCheck.org has tracked as years of mixed messaging on the shot.

events.title: 2026 cases top 1,000 within two months
events.detail: US confirmed measles cases surpassed 1,000 by late February 2026 (1,136 cases as of Feb 26), a pace far outstripping the prior year and prompting CNN's public health desk to warn that 'expect more deaths' as the outbreak accelerated nationally beyond its original Southwest epicenter.

events.title: West Virginia lawmakers introduce broad exemption bill
events.detail: West Virginia legislators introduced House Bill 4947, which would codify religious, conscientious, and personal exemptions from the state's compulsory school immunization law — one of the strictest in the country. The bill was referred to committee and had not been enacted as of mid-2026, even as the governor's administrative exemption process continued operating in parallel.

events.title: South Carolina declares its outbreak over
events.detail: South Carolina declared the end of its measles outbreak in April 2026, after a run from October 2025 that totaled nearly 1,000 cases, the large majority in unvaccinated residents, making it briefly the largest single-state outbreak of the resurgence.

events.title: Reporting discrepancies highlight national undercount problem
events.detail: Analysts flagged sharp discrepancies between CDC's national dashboard and state/media counts — e.g., Florida case totals ranged from 64 (CDC) to 68 (media reports) to 92 (CNN's independent tracker) — underscoring that the CDC publishes only laboratory-confirmed cases as of a weekly Thursday cutoff, while state dashboards often run ahead. Officials in South Carolina and Texas separately said the true scope of household transmission was 'impossible to know.'

events.title: Hospitalization rate falls even as case count hits 35-year high
events.detail: CDC surveillance data showed the share of measles patients hospitalized fell to 7% in 2026 from 11% in 2025, even as total case counts hit a 35-year high — attributed partly to greater clinical awareness and faster outpatient management. Children age 5 and under, who made up 19% of 2026 cases, still faced a notably higher 10% hospitalization rate. Overall, 93% of patients were unvaccinated or had unknown vaccination status.

events.title: Utah health official: outbreak now the state's longest on record
events.detail: Marking roughly a year since Utah's outbreak began, a state health official said it was among the largest in the nation and 'definitely the longest' in Utah's modern history, with case totals climbing past 700 combined across 2025-2026.

events.title: National case count tops 2,500
events.detail: With 101 new cases reported in a single week, the 2026 national total surpassed 2,500 confirmed cases, extending the worst measles year in the US since 1991 into its final stretch before the November PAHO status decision.

events.title: CDC confirms 2,465 cases as elimination review convenes
events.detail: The US National Verification Committee for the Elimination of Measles, Rubella, and Congenital Rubella Syndrome, chaired by Noel Brewer, reviewed CDC's annual measles report in mid-August 2026 with the national case count at 2,465. The US has recorded measles cases every week since January 2025 — roughly 20 straight months of transmission. The committee's assessment will be forwarded to PAHO, with a formal decision on US elimination status due in November 2026.

events.title: National total jumps to 2,777 as Pennsylvania and Ohio surge
events.detail: CDC's Aug 20, 2026 weekly update added 211 new confirmed cases — more than double the prior week's +101 gain — bringing the 2026 national total to 2,777 across 47 jurisdictions, with 94% (2,614 of 2,777) outbreak-associated. Most new cases were concentrated in Pennsylvania and Ohio, where the state's fourth 2026 outbreak (Sugarcreek/Bloomfield area) pushed Ohio's yearly total to 142 cases, a jump of 73 in a single week.

media.caption: CDC adds 211 new cases to accelerating US measles outbreak

events.title: Pennsylvania reports the nation's first 2026 measles deaths
events.detail: The Pennsylvania Department of Health announced Aug 25, 2026 that 2 unvaccinated Lancaster County residents had died with measles — the state's first measles deaths in 35 years and the first confirmed 2026 deaths nationally. One was an infant who tested positive for measles and died of a splenic laceration; the state declined to disclose further identifying details, including ages, locations, or whether the individuals were part of Lancaster's Plain communities, citing patient privacy. Lancaster County has recorded 185 cases in 2026, one of the largest outbreaks in the country; statewide Pennsylvania has 393 cases across 29 counties.

media.caption: Measles-related deaths in Pennsylvania mark first 2 US fatalities this year

events.title: CDC publicly disputes Pennsylvania's framing of its measles deaths
events.detail: Two days after Pennsylvania's death announcement, CDC said 'these discrepancies raise important questions, particularly because the Governor's Office has not provided CDC with information relevant to the outbreak and has declined our offers of assistance,' adding that under Trump and RFK Jr.'s leadership 'CDC will follow the facts and tell the American people the truth.' The Lancaster County coroner's office said it had not confirmed any deaths caused BY measles, only that it was reviewing an infant death with a positive measles test — while Pennsylvania officials maintained their 'measles-associated' terminology reflects standard practice when lab or epidemiologic evidence of measles is present, regardless of the medical examiner's cause-of-death finding.
events.confidenceReason: CDC and Pennsylvania state officials publicly disagree on whether measles was the cause of death in either case; the county coroner has not issued a final determination.

media.caption: 'Tell the American people the truth': CDC responds to Shapiro, 'measles-related' deaths

events.title: Seneca County, NY outbreak declared amid Upstate New York cluster growth
events.detail: Seneca County Public Health Director Scott King said Aug 27, 2026 that 5 confirmed measles cases plus dozens of probable illnesses met the state definition of an outbreak; 2 of the 5 confirmed patients were hospitalized. The cluster, traced to a resident's travel to Pennsylvania, is part of a broader Upstate New York surge to more than 20 confirmed cases across Seneca, Madison, and Allegheny counties in a matter of weeks. County health staff have expanded home-visit MMR vaccination efforts.

media.caption: Measles in Seneca County meets outbreak definition
